title: Sanctions-adjacent supplier payment hold creates supply disruption
scenario_pattern: Geopolitical shock increases sanctions risk. Treasury considers payment hold. Supplier threatens shipment hold. Legal requires ownership screening. Procurement has short inventory runway. Accounting may need disclosure if disruption crosses materiality.
outcome: Decision should be framed as payment/legal/supply trade-off, not isolated sanctions or treasury issue.

title: Cash trapped in affected subsidiary after capital control announcement
scenario_pattern: A subsidiary holds book cash in a jurisdiction where capital controls are announced. Group treasury wants to fund another region but transfer route and local permission are unknown.
outcome: Treat cash as uncertain availability until transfer route is confirmed; exclude from unrestricted liquidity in stress case.

title: Critical supplier payment due within 10 days during bank disruption
scenario_pattern: Payment is due soon to a critical supplier. Beneficiary bank is in an affected country. Payment could be delayed by sanctions screening or bank closure; supplier may stop shipment if unpaid.
outcome: Escalate Treasury/Legal/Procurement joint review; do not issue single-mode payment recommendation.

title: Alternative payment route changes risk profile
scenario_pattern: Original payment route is disrupted. Alternative route uses another group entity and currency, creating FX, tax, sanctions and contract questions.
outcome: Alternative routes should be options with risk annotations, not automatic recommendations.

title: Counterparty ownership chain incomplete in sanctions-exposed jurisdiction
scenario_pattern: Counterparty is not on an official sanctions list, but beneficial ownership data is incomplete and one upstream owner resembles a blocked person name.
outcome: High-confidence clearance is not appropriate; beneficial ownership and official list screening are required.

title: Force majeure considered without notice deadline
scenario_pattern: A supplier disruption may excuse performance, but the force majeure clause and notice deadline are not available.
outcome: AI should flag potential relevance but avoid stating force majeure applies; contract review required.

title: Last-minute bank account change before payment
scenario_pattern: Supplier requests last-minute change in payment bank, route and beneficiary details during geopolitical event.
outcome: Treat as red flag for sanctions/fraud/export-control review; pause automated payment advice pending review.

title: Regulatory investigation may create provision or contingent liability
scenario_pattern: A regulator inquiry is announced after alleged past conduct. Management cannot estimate outcome, but potential penalties are material.
outcome: Frame as provision/contingent liability review; map evidence to present obligation, probable outflow and reliable estimate.

title: Major event after reporting date before authorization
scenario_pattern: Major customer cancellation occurs after reporting date but before financial statements are authorized. Facts indicate deteriorating conditions may have existed before period end.
outcome: Subsequent event assessment should determine adjusting versus non-adjusting treatment based on conditions at reporting date.

title: Flood damages plant and changes cash-flow outlook
scenario_pattern: A major plant flood reduces capacity for months. Fixed assets and inventory are material; recoverable amount may fall.
outcome: Flag impairment and inventory valuation review; request asset/CGU carrying amount and forecast sensitivity.

title: Single-source component disrupted by natural disaster
scenario_pattern: A critical component is sourced from one supplier in an affected region. Alternative source exists but is not approved and qualification takes months.
outcome: Supplier substitution friction is high; decision should focus on inventory runway, customer prioritization and qualification acceleration.

title: Tier-1 supplier unaffected but sub-tier material concentrated
scenario_pattern: Tier-1 supplier reports no disruption, but underlying material is likely sourced from a region affected by export restrictions.
outcome: Sub-tier unknown should be treated as significant; generate hypotheses and ask procurement for BOM/sub-tier confirmation.

title: Port closure extends inbound shipment lead time
scenario_pattern: Port closure delays inbound shipments. Inventory runway is below the estimated rerouting lead time, and expedited freight has large cost impact.
outcome: Procurement, Treasury and Accounting should coordinate route choice, cost approval and possible customer commitments.

title: Critical service may breach tolerance before data is complete
scenario_pattern: External disruption may interrupt an important business service. Dependency map is incomplete, but time-to-impact is shorter than data confirmation cycle.
outcome: Executive decision should preserve optionality and assign owners for missing data confirmation within deadline.
